headline: Trade {price.prod.f64.persona.gain|abs|pts} points on {aspects.persona.name} for {price.prod.f64.persona.cost_gap|usd_per_1k} in savings.
lede: {arm:f64} saves {cost.uplift.f64|abs|pct} on cost while clearing all guardrails, but drops {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}) on {aspects.persona.name}. The decision rests on whether character consistency losses in extended turns justify the monthly budget reduction.

slots.text: {arm:f64} cuts cost by {price.prod.f64.persona.cost_gap|usd_per_1k} ({price.prod.f64.persona.monthly_cost_gap|usd_whole} per month) but trails {arm:prod} on {aspects.persona.name} by {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}).
{arm:f64} is favored when a point on {aspects.persona.name} is worth less than {price.prod.f64.persona.per_point|usd} per 1,000 replies; above that, {arm:prod} remains preferable.
Lean toward {arm:f64} if monthly infrastructure cost reduction takes precedence over character fidelity in conversations exceeding five turns.
A user-preference study measuring churn or satisfaction in conversations beyond five turns would settle whether persona degradation affects engagement.

method.text: Tested across {scoreboard.prod.cases} cases with repeats yielding {scoreboard.prod.ran} total trials per arm.
